Intel HD Graphics 5500 benchmark: What games can it run?
I just saw a good sale on a HD Graphics 5500 laptop, so I went looking for this information. This article seemed pretty useful. Anyone on here play games on an HD 5500?

At 1080p, which is largely the standard on most laptops you will be fairly limited. You would be able to run non-GPU intensive games like Civilization 5 or Cities: Skylines reasonable well until you get to late game where you might notice some hitching or lag. You can also play a large quantity of indie games like Super Meat Boy or Don't Starve. If you are expecting any sort of AAA performance out of integrated graphics you will be disappointed. Unless you are willing to bottom out graphical settings, including lowering your resolution below what your monitor naively supports (which is really tough to play through) you will not be able to play the really popular triple A games with lots of textures and expansive worlds. Even a low level discrete GPU will beat out the 5500 in most cases so if you can I would suggest splurging on a nicer GPU if it is within your budget. If you are set on this laptop that is on sale I will paste in some benchmarks in popular games as well as an article which gives a full review.

Triple A Games* * The Witcher 3: 4 fps @ 1080p (average), 9 fps @ 1366x768 * GTA V: 5 fps @ 1080p (average), 19 fps @ 768p * Far Cry 4: 6fps @ 1080p (average), 11 fps @ 768p

Top Downs, 4x, Turn-Based * Civilization: Beyond Earth 11 fps @ 1080p, 17fps @ 768p

Notebook Check is a bit harsh with their benchmarks in that they don't tell you the whole graphical settings they use and in truth you could probably achieve higher fps if you are willing to make more sacrifices in visual fidelity, but those decisions on where to cut should be done on an individual basis that is tolerable for you.

Source: http://www.notebookcheck.net/Intel-HD-Graphics-5500.125586.0.html

In Short: yes, you can "game" with 5500 graphics but you are pretty limited and will need to curb your expectations
Yeah, I'm willing to use low quality graphics to run games.
